# Specialisations

**Goal:** Ship **boot-menu alternate configurations** from one flake host using NixOS `specialisation.<name>.configuration`, know how to activate them at runtime vs reboot, and when a specialisation beats a second container or VM.

NixOS **26.05** (“Yarara”) keeps specialisations as first-class boot entries built beside the parent system. Channel Nix is typically **2.34.x**; many desks run Nix CLI **2.35+** via `nix.package` — specialisations do not depend on that split, but pin your notes to `nixos-version` / `nix --version` on the lab.

## Mental model

```text
nixosConfigurations.lab
        │
        ▼
 parent system closure  (default boot entry)
        │
        ├── specialisation.nvidia.configuration  →  extra closure + boot submenu entry
        ├── specialisation.rescue.configuration →  …
        └── …
                │
                ▼
 /run/current-system/specialisation/<name>/bin/switch-to-configuration
```

| Piece | Role |
|-------|------|
| `specialisation.<name>.configuration` | Nested NixOS module(s) for the variant |
| `inheritParentConfig` (default `true`) | Merge on top of the parent; `false` = build from scratch |
| Boot loader entries | Choose the specialisation at boot (kernel/initrd differences need reboot) |
| `nixos-rebuild switch --specialisation <name>` | Activate that variant after a rebuild |
| `/run/current-system/specialisation/<name>/…` | Switch without a full rebuild when the closure already exists |
| Nested specialisations | **Ignored** — do not nest |

Names must **not** contain `/`.

## When to use vs containers / second hosts

| Need | Prefer |
|------|--------|
| Same machine, same disks, alternate kernel / drivers / desktop / “laptop on battery vs docked GPU” | **Specialisation** |
| Strong isolation, different OS, throwaway rootfs | **Container** or VM |
| Long-lived second identity with different networking policy | Separate `nixosConfigurations` host or VM |
| One-off package test | `nix shell` / vm test — not a specialisation |

Specialisations still share the machine’s hardware and usually much of the store; they are **configuration variants**, not security boundaries.

## Worked examples

### Case 1: GPU-off by default, GPU-on specialisation

Parent keeps heavy drivers off with `mkDefault` so the child can flip them:

```nix
# hosts/lab/specialisations-gpu.nix
{ lib, pkgs, ... }:

{
  # Parent desk: drivers off unless a specialisation overrides
  hardware.nvidia.modesetting.enable = lib.mkDefault false;

  specialisation.nvidia = {
    configuration = {
      system.nixos.tags = [ "nvidia" ];
      hardware.nvidia.modesetting.enable = true;
      # Add the rest of your NVIDIA module stack here as you already do on a GPU host
    };
  };
}
```

Import that file from the host module list. Rebuild:

```bash
sudo nixos-rebuild switch --flake .#lab
# Boot menu should offer a specialised entry tagged/named for nvidia
```

Runtime activate (userspace switch — **does not reload the kernel**):

```bash
sudo nixos-rebuild switch --flake .#lab --specialisation nvidia
# Or, if already built into the current system:
sudo /run/current-system/specialisation/nvidia/bin/switch-to-configuration switch
```

If the specialisation changes the **kernel** or early initrd modules, reboot and pick the boot entry; a userspace switch will not magically load the other kernel.

### Case 2: Independent specialisation (`inheritParentConfig = false`)

```nix
# hosts/lab/specialisation-kiosk.nix
{ pkgs, ... }:

{
  specialisation.kiosk = {
    inheritParentConfig = false;
    configuration = {
      system.nixos.tags = [ "kiosk" ];
      imports = [ ./kiosk-baseline.nix ];
      users.users.kiosk = {
        isNormalUser = true;
        extraGroups = [ "video" ];
      };
      services.displayManager.autoLogin = {
        enable = true;
        user = "kiosk";
      };
      environment.systemPackages = with pkgs; [ chromium ];
    };
  };
}
```

Use this when the variant should **not** inherit desk services, VPN, or extra users from the parent. You own the full module closure — easy to under-specify boot/networking; test on a disposable VM first.

### Case 3: Parent-only config (not pulled into children)

When `specialisation != {}`, you can attach options that apply to the **default** system only:

```nix
# modules/parent-only-opengl.nix
{ lib, config, pkgs, ... }:

{
  config = lib.mkIf (config.specialisation != { }) {
    # Example: keep a parent-only package set out of specialised closures
    environment.systemPackages = lib.mkBefore [ pkgs.pciutils ];
  };
}
```

If **no** specialisations exist, `config.specialisation != {}` is false — do not rely on this pattern to mean “always on the default host” in a config with zero specialisations.

### Case 4: Inspect built specialisations

```bash
ls -la /run/current-system/specialisation/
readlink -f /run/current-system/specialisation/nvidia
nixos-version
nix --version
```

After `switch`, confirm tags:

```bash
cat /run/current-system/nixos-version
# specialised systems often carry system.nixos.tags in the banner / labels you set
```

## Activation cheat sheet

| Action | Command |
|--------|---------|
| Build parent + all specialisations | `sudo nixos-rebuild switch --flake .#lab` |
| Switch into one by name | `sudo nixos-rebuild switch --flake .#lab --specialisation <name>` |
| Switch using already-built path | `sudo /run/current-system/specialisation/<name>/bin/switch-to-configuration switch` |
| Test without adding a boot generation the same way you usually `test` | Prefer `switch-to-configuration test` on that path when experimenting |
| Kernel / initrd divergent | **Reboot** into the boot-menu entry |

Plain `nixos-rebuild switch` without `--specialisation` returns you to the **parent** default — a common surprise after you had activated a child.

## The trap

**Trap A — treat specialisations like containers.** They do not isolate failures or untrusted workloads.

**Trap B — expect `switch --specialisation` to change the running kernel.** Boot-menu reboot required for kernel/initrd.

**Trap C — override parent booleans without `mkDefault` on the parent.** The merge may not let the child win; set parent defaults with `lib.mkDefault`.

**Trap D — nest specialisations.** Nested entries are ignored; flatten the matrix or use separate hosts.

**Trap E — huge Cartesian products.** Each specialisation is another system closure to build and store; prefer two or three named modes, not a dozen.

## Try this

1. Add a `specialisation.demo.configuration` that only sets `environment.variables.DEMO = "1";` and `system.nixos.tags`.
2. `nixos-rebuild switch`, then activate with `--specialisation demo` and `echo $DEMO` in a new login.
3. Change a kernel package in the specialisation on a **VM**, reboot into the entry, confirm `uname -r`.
4. Document on the rollback card: how to get back to the parent (`switch` without `--specialisation` + reboot if needed).
